claims.claim: CAPACITY CONTROL. The slot architecture can express a largely tracker-like view: trained to imitate the tracker's segmentation (sam_sup, 3000 steps) it reaches ARI 0.85 against the tracker on the half it was not fitted on, about 1.2 slots per tracked object, leaves about a third of its 12 slots empty (the tracker has 7.4 objects per frame), and the matched slot's mass follows the object's mass.

NO OBJECTS FROM THE OBJECTIVES. With the geometric encoder (which starts as soft k-means) every unsupervised objective ends at the k-means parts, not at the tracker's objects: closure (sam_set), closure with the dead-direction term (sam_set_dg), local law (sam_self) and reconstruction (sam_rec) all give ARI 0.63 against the tracker, 2.1 slots per tracked object, all 12 slots in use, high precision and low recall (a slot lies inside one object, an object is split over slots), matched-slot mass unrelated to the object's mass, position recovered. The no-learning soft k-means km_s3 has the same numbers. [checker] The encoders do not start at km_s3 but at the sigma = 6 k-means with fewer iterations: the untrained encoder scores ARI 0.72 against the tracker and 0.95 against km_s6 (pilot r5-slots-003, sam_set_dg rows, which are initial weights; a different realisation of the same seeds). In this run km_s6 scores 0.72, km_s6w 0.72 and the 12 fixed regions (grid) 0.65 against the tracker. Training on any of the four objectives therefore LOWERS the agreement with the tracker by about 0.09, to the level of the narrower k-means km_s3 and below the fixed grid; km_s3 is the k-means variant that matched afterwards, not the start. On this ARI scale 'no object information' is 0.63-0.72 and the supervised control 0.85.

THE OBJECTIVES LEAVE THE TRACKER-LIKE VIEW. Started from the supervised encoder (encoder frozen for the first 375 steps while the new head warms up), each objective walks back to the parts: recall + purity of the masks against the tracker on held-out trajectories (2 = the tracker's segmentation) is 1.87 at the start, 1.71 at step 500, 1.65 at step 1000 and stays there, the value of the cold-started encoders; the certified agreement of the warm-started encoders equals that of the cold-started ones. So the tracker-like view is not a minimum that the optimiser failed to find from a k-means start. [checker] The move is driven by the objective: the closure value of sam_set_ws on the held-out trajectories is 0.43 with the tracker-like encoder frozen and the head warmed up (step 300), 0.28 at step 1000 and 0.24 at step 3000, while recall + purity falls (it was 0.44 and 0.43 at steps 200 and 300, so the fall is not the head still warming up). Limits: recall + purity is measured on 4 held-out trajectories per replica (4 replicas); the warm-started encoders are certified from checkpoints chosen after step 750, that is after the walk back; and the tracker-like view is fragile under its own supervised objective too: one of the four sam_sup replicas (fit B, seed 1) oscillated between 1.61 and 1.87 after step 1200 (1.61 at step 1500, 1.87 at step 2000, 1.70 at step 3000) and is certified from its step-900 checkpoint (the 1.82 quoted for sam_sup at step 3000 is the mean including it; the other three are at 1.85-1.86).

CLOSURE RANKS THE PARTS ABOVE THE OBJECTS. Each view judged in its own coordinates with the same permutation-equivariant predictor family (S: shared linear rule and shared attention network over slots; 6 numbers per slot = mass, position, size; h = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16; SE 0.01-0.02): the tracker's object view has the lowest ceiling of the object-like views, the supervised tracker-like encoder is in between, the parts (k-means or any objective-trained encoder) are highest; only the fixed grid is lower than the tracker at long horizons. [checker] Paired by certification trajectory (checker's bootstrap over the 32 trajectories, from out/items/*.npz): km_s3 minus the tracker is +0.05, +0.17, +0.39 at h = 1, 4, 16 (z 5, 7, 21), the supervised encoder minus the tracker +0.24 at h = 16 (z 18). The eight cold-started encoders do not differ from km_s3 at any horizon (|difference| <= 0.01, |z| <= 1.8); against km_s6, the bandwidth they start from (0.96 / 0.83 / 0.48 at h = 1 / 4 / 16), sam_set is +0.08 at h = 8 and 16 (z 4 to 5). km_s3 is the best of the three k-means variants at h = 16 (km_s6w 0.55) and became the reference after the results. The views compared have different slot counts (12 parts, 7.4 objects with empty slots as zeros) in a slot-indexed layout, and the same measure puts a frozen code highest (sac_set 0.90 at h = 16), so a higher ceiling alone does not make a view the better description.

PREDICTABLE CONTENT. The parts also hold more predictable nats per frame in the same 72 numbers (captured by family S). Diagonal Gaussian measure at h = 1 / 4 / 16: 200 / 102 / 29 for km_s3 against 111 / 43 / 5 for the tracker's view. Log-det measure at h = 1: 192 against 81, with the supervised encoder in between (119); the tracker's log-det is ill-conditioned at longer horizons (empty slots make its covariance nearly singular; its available content is undefined), so only h = 1 is quoted for it. The diagonal measure counts redundant coordinates repeatedly (the collapsed sgm_set scores highest on it, and negative on the log-det), so it is quoted here only for views whose slots are distinct. [checker] The tracker's log-det value at h = 1 is the mean of two halves that disagree (58 and 103); at h = 4 half A is negative (-26); so 81 is known to about +-23 only. 'The same 72 numbers' counts the tracker's empty slots: the parts have 12 present slots against 7.4 (ratio 1.6), and the ratio of diagonal content is 1.8 at h = 1, 2.4 at h = 4 and 5.9 at h = 16, so at h = 1 most of the gap is the slot count and the excess per slot appears at the longer horizons. On the diagonal measure the tracker's view holds about what the fixed grid holds (124 / 40 / 2).

THE OBJECTIVES THEMSELVES PREFER THE PARTS. Value of each objective on each frozen view, with a fresh head trained for 1000 steps (lower is better; mean of 4 replicas): closure and local law score the tracker's view worst of the object-like views (0.45), the supervised tracker-like encoder next (0.42), k-means parts 0.32-0.35 and the objective-trained encoders 0.28-0.31; reconstruction also prefers parts (0.47) to the tracker's view (0.55). Whether training improves the objective beyond k-means (0.29 against 0.32-0.35 in this run) is not resolved (checker's note below). Between runs the tracker's closure value moves by about 0.05 (0.49 in r5-slots-007, a different simulation), far less than the gap. [checker] Each value is measured on 4 held-out trajectories per half, the ones on which the trained encoders' checkpoints were selected. Under the same protocol (1000 head steps) a fixed view's value moves by up to 0.04 between runs: km_s6 0.317 in r5-slots-007 and 0.353 here, km_s3 0.337 and 0.321 (their order flips), the tracker 0.493 and 0.453. The values also depend on the head's budget: with 300 head steps (pilot r5-slots-003) the tracker scored 0.577, km_s3 0.332, km_s6 0.325 and the trained sam_set 0.334 (no gain over k-means). The order tracker > supervised > parts holds in all three runs and under the dead-direction term (objective_values.*.set.mean_guarded); the tracker's gap to the parts (0.10-0.25) is the robust part of this claim. That the encoders do move 'which matter a slot holds' is shown under claim 1 (from the sigma-6 start to the km_s3-like parts).

WHAT THE TRACKER'S LOGIC ADDS: INDIVIDUATION AND EVENTS. The tracker says how many objects there are (one per connected blob) and re-labels at once when blobs fuse or split; this world has about 67-71 fusions and about as many fissions per 300-tick trajectory for 7.4 objects (corrected by the checker: 131-138 is the number of slot rows that carry the fission flag, and the tracker flags both the parent and the product of a fission, vw/objects.py; 68-71 slots per trajectory are absorbed by fusions and, with births and deaths near zero and a stationary count, as many are created by fissions). The parts keep all 12 slots in use and never merge: just after a fusion the best slot holds 0.42 of the fused object and still only 0.72 more than 16 ticks later, while after a fission recall is 0.79 at once. The supervised encoder learned to empty slots (8.0 present) and to merge, but with a lag of 4 to 8 ticks after either event (recall 0.69 at a fusion and 0.67 at a fission, 0.93-0.96 by ticks 8-15). Each objective scores those jumps as unpredictable change of the slot numbers, which is what it is asked to avoid.

COLLAPSE WITHOUT THE GEOMETRIC PRIOR OR THE MOMENT READOUT. Plain slot attention under closure (sgm_set, no k-means distance term) collapses to 12 identical slots that each take a twelfth of everything: ARI 0.00, 12 slots per object, closure value 0.02, about 6 effective dimensions in 72 numbers, negative captured log-det content, both seeds identical. A learned 6-number code under closure (sac_set, k-means masks kept) becomes a nearly frozen code: about 1.6 effective dimensions, probes of mass, position and velocity at R2 0.00, ceiling 0.90 at h = 16, non-finite objective values. The joint-covariance metric did not stop either (directions below its ridge drop out of the loss); the dead-direction term was only run with the moment readout, where there is no collapse to prevent. The classic slot-attention autoencoder (sgc_rec) finds neither objects nor a stable view (ARI 0.28, 6.5 slots per object, seed-pair ARI 0.16); a reconstruction-trained code on k-means masks (sac_rec) carries little about the objects (mass probe R2 0.06).

SEED STABILITY AND REPLICATION. The parts are a stable outcome: two seeds fitted on the same half agree (hard segmentations: ARI 0.91-0.94; matched slots' numbers: R2 0.81-0.90), and all sit at ARI 0.80 against the no-learning km_s6 (checker: the untrained encoder is at 0.95 against km_s6 and its two seeds at 1.00 against each other, pilot's sam_set_dg rows, so 0.80 measures how far training moved the masks from their start, and part of the seed agreement is inherited from the shared deterministic start). Three GPU runs with different simulations (GPU float64 is not bit-deterministic) give the same picture: the pilot's sam_set (600 steps, H200), the failed run's supervised encoder and references (2000 steps), and this run. [checker] The three runs share the designer seeds 9801 / 9802; they differ through GPU non-determinism (objects per frame in half A: 7.39, 7.54, 7.40), so they are different realisations of the same ensemble, not independent seeds.

review.source: code review by the Mac runner, relayed by the coordinator on 9 Nov 2026 (after r5-slots-003 was requested; the pilot r5-slots-003 runs the code before these fixes, pinned by ref e5d146ef3)

items.finding: validation encoded N_VAL x 301 ticks x 4 replicas in one call; the 3 x 3 token concat built f32[4, 8, 301, 32, 32, 288] = 2.84e9 elements, above 2^31
items.fix: snets.make_encoder.tokens: the 3 x 3 neighbourhood is nine block matmuls (same weights, same map; max abs difference 1.2e-6 against the concat form on CPU), so no (frames, tokens, 288) array exists; strain.trainer.val encodes one validation trajectory at a time (lax.map); level 0, branches and label maps are one device array per half (largest 9.5e8 elements at full size, before 1.89e9 for the stacked pair); strain.fits() records every large planned shape and refuses any above 2^31 - 1 elements; the largest are written to train_done.json (largest_device_arrays)

items.finding: an encoder cut by the deadline before STEPS // 4 was certified with its initial weights
items.fix: strain.train_config: a replica without a checkpoint takes the weights at the cut if their validation value is finite (checkpoint 'last'), otherwise it is not certified (checkpoint 'none', the config is reported as failed); 'checkpoint', 'cut_by_deadline' and 'steps_planned' are stored with every Phi (CPU test: a cut at step 10 of 80 gives 'last' for all four replicas)

items.finding: the certification workers' own time limit could exceed the runner's kill time
items.fix: job.sh: the workers are killed at S5_HARD_S seconds from the start of the script (default S5_CERT_S + 300, before S5_CERT_S + 900); the request sets it below max_hours with margin for pooling and collection; killed workers and unclaimed items are counted in progress.txt and cert_incomplete.json

items.finding: DONE marker, getmtime race, GPU-backend check in the job script
items.fix: job.sh writes the DONE marker itself after strain.py exits, whatever its exit code (a crash at import no longer leaves the workers waiting); scert.claim tolerates a marker renamed by another worker between the listing and getmtime; job.sh refuses to run when jax.default_backend() is not 'gpu' unless S5_ALLOW_CPU=1

items.finding: 'stopcarry' was a no-op (the state entering a window is already detached)
items.fix: snets.make_encoder.tick_carry: with stopcarry the carried memory enters EVERY tick without gradient (no backpropagation through time); checked on CPU: same values, different gradients (relative squared difference 0.16)

checker.who: independent checker of round-5 study slots (worktree wt-slotschk), 10 Nov 2026; no GPU job run; about 3 CPU-minutes (nice 10, one thread); own code read origin/gpu-jobs:jobs/r5-slots-00{3,7,8}/ (combined.json, cert/*.json, items/*.npz, train/*.json, objval/*.json, masks/*.npz, sim_*.json, status.json, logs)
checker.verdict: The numbers hold; some of the wording did not. All 183 claim values re-resolve from the job files (max deviation 5e-5), every table entry of the report recomputes from the per-half certification files and the per-item errors, the job records and the bill match, the code at ref 7099a0ded is what the report describes, no secret is committed. The main direction is supported for this architecture: no objective produced the tracker's objects, all four moved a tracker-like start back to parts while their loss fell, and the tracker's view is less closed than the parts by a wide margin (ceiling at h = 16 0.17 against 0.56, paired z 21). Corrections: (1) the fission count was doubled (about 68-71 per trajectory, not 131-138); (2) the trained encoders did not stay at k-means: they start at the sigma-6 k-means (ARI 0.72 against the tracker) and training lowers that to 0.63, the level of km_s3 and below a fixed grid (0.65), which the report's table does not show (of the k-means variants it lists km_s3 only); (3) 'training improves the objective beyond k-means' is not resolved (0.03-0.06 against a run-to-run movement of up to 0.04, none in the pilot); (4) the tracker's log-det content at h = 1 (81) averages two halves at 58 and 103; (5) at h = 1 most of the 'more predictable nats' is the slot count (12 against 7.4); (6) 'designer's convention' and 'individuation must be supplied' are readings, not results: no parsimony or connectivity term was run, and the closure measures used also rank a frozen code and a collapsed view highest.

findings.what: 131-138 'fissions per trajectory' counts flagged slot rows (parent and product); the number of fissions is about that of fusions, 68-71 per trajectory. Fixed in claims[6]; the README and the report still say 131-138.

The cold-started encoders start at the sigma-6 k-means (ARI 0.72 against the tracker; km_s6 0.72, km_s6w 0.72, grid 0.65). Every objective moved them to the km_s3-like parts at 0.63. So training made the agreement with the tracker worse than no training, and 'ARI 0.63' is not above a fixed grid. This strengthens 'the objectives prefer parts' and replaces 'the same numbers as soft k-means' by 'the numbers of the narrower of the k-means variants tried'.

'Training improves the objective a little beyond k-means (0.29 against 0.32)': the difference is of the size of the run-to-run movement of a fixed view under the same protocol, the order of km_s3 and km_s6 flips between r5-slots-007 and 008, the pilot shows no gain, and the values are from 4 held-out trajectories per half that also selected the checkpoints. Reworded in claims[5].

The objective values depend on the head's budget (tracker 0.58 at 300 head steps, 0.45-0.49 at 1000); no convergence check exists. The order tracker > supervised > parts is the same at both budgets and in the independent certification.

The tracker-like view is fragile: under its own objective one of four supervised replicas oscillated between recall + purity 1.61 and 1.87 after step 1200; the other three stayed at 1.80 or more from step 1100 on. The warm-start result still stands: 16 of 16 replicas are at 1.72 or below within 425 steps of the unfreezing, with a falling loss, and none comes back (at most 1.70 from step 1000 on). 'Not a minimum the optimiser missed' is shown for these four objectives with this covariance guard; a control that continues the supervised objective from the same start was not run.

Predictable content: the tracker's log-det at h = 1 is 58 in one half and 103 in the other; the available content of the reference view is undefined in half A at every horizon. Recommending the log-det measure (decision 4 of the report) needs more branches per item or a regularised estimate before it can rank views with empty slots.

'The tracker's object view is a designer's convention' and 'individuation must be supplied' are interpretations. What is measured: in a slot-indexed layout with K = 12, fixed-count parts are more closed than 7.4 objects with event jumps. No parsimony, connectivity or slot-count term was run, K was not varied, and no set-matched (identity-free) score was used; the same closure measures rank a frozen code (sac_set) and a collapsed view (sgm_set) highest.

Only encoders that start at k-means or at the supervised encoder gave a usable view; the two encoders without the k-means distance term collapsed (sgm_set) or were unstable (sgc_rec, per-replica ARI 0.10-0.53). 'Objectives end at parts' is therefore tested from two starting points of one architecture, on one level-0 theory, with public parameters.

km_s3 (ceilings 0.97 / 0.87 / 0.56) is the best of three k-means variants at h = 16 and was chosen as 'the' soft k-means after the results; km_s6 has 0.96 / 0.83 / 0.48. As a level-1 candidate it has not been tested under inputs or with an agent.
